grand_strategy.reading: Hezbollah in October 2026 is a movement that has lost the war it was built to deter and has not yet lost the argument that justifies its weapons. Luttwak's logic shows twice. First, deterrence is a paradoxical good: an arsenal big enough to frighten Israel was also big enough to make destroying it Israel's priority, and the 'support front' of October 2023 handed Jerusalem the moment. Second, relational manoeuvre - the hidden, dispersed, community-embedded network, tied to Iran by a land bridge - beat Israeli firepower for eighteen years until Israeli intelligence penetrated the network itself: the pagers of 17 September 2024 and the decapitation that followed were less a military victory than the demonstration that the network had been read. Since then its position is that of a besieged political party with an army: the land route through Syria is shut by a hostile neighbour, Iranian cash comes by courier, the Lebanese state has banned its military activity and signed a framework that trades Israeli withdrawal for its disarmament, and its constituency is displaced and occupied. What keeps it from collapse is not strength but structure: a confessional system that cannot decide against the Shia community, an army that will not fight it, Amal as a brake on the state, and an Israeli occupation that supplies the justification. The open question for the next stage is whether the Lebanese state, with Gulf, US and European money behind its army, can turn the pilot zones into a precedent without provoking the clash both sides say they want to avoid, or whether Israel's tunnels-and-demolition campaign forces Hezbollah to choose between its arms and its place in the state.

stances.note: Hezbollah needs the state and resists alignment with it. It sits in the Salam cabinet (a Hezbollah minister reportedly approved the 2 March 2026 ban), told Al Jazeera the same day that it acknowledges the government's right to decide on war and peace, puts the onus on Beirut for reconstruction money, defends the army from 'humiliation' (15 Aug 2026) and has never fought it. Against that it treated the cabinet decision of Aug 2025 'as if it did not exist', walked out three times, threatens a 'Karbala-like' battle and demands the 2026 framework's 'downfall'. Why not rival: the cooperation is structural (the Shia share of the system, state cover, donor money) and no source has Hezbollah targeting state institutions; Lebanon's own card grades Hezbollah rival, an asymmetry that is deliberate. It becomes a rival if the army moves by force or Hezbollah leaves the cabinet. No source uses the label; our reading, confidence C. Bond - kin: the same citizens and the same confessional system.

Two Amal ministers and one Hezbollah minister reportedly approved; Hezbollah's bloc leader Raad called it 'rash'. Hezbollah fired on Israel the same day.

relations_to.summary: Hezbollah fired on Israel on 2 March 2026 for Iran after the killing of Khamenei, ending the November 2024 ceasefire; Israel struck Beirut and began a ground campaign on 16 March.
